name: voidsquid
description: The game engine of the Void family, on Void Core and Void Maiz: a studio for building new worlds out of the games a person owns (load a game, inspect and tag what came out, lay out tables, set the feast, play), and a forge that will pour one document into many artifacts. It began as the host Void Jelly cannot be for itself, and still is.
status_note: 0.1.0 (2026-10-12): the first real version of the studio. A docked Void Maiz window (Turkey, Table, Feast, Data and Scene workspaces; Shelf, Inspector, Console, Load a game, Setup) over a .squid project, which is a Void Core state document; a game library's catalogue (assets.db, Void Hormiga's schema) imported as mantles, every edit a dispatcher command; Load a game (recon plus a catalogue of known decompilations, deterministic); a setup inventory (minimum, local model, vision, agent). Rung 2.5's .ink harness is the Scene workspace. Nothing builds for a constrained target yet (rung 3); the game model is still design only (S14).

requires.name: voidjelly
requires.note: the 3D library: owns .ink, nibs, emitters, residuals and every geometry computation. Void Squid is its first host and performs every effect it refuses to; Squid computes nothing about geometry and never parses .ink directly. The contract between the two repositories is the .ink format, which Jelly defines in its provides.documents; it is described here once, on the requires edge, because mago doctor notes that a requires edge plus an interacts_with entry for the same pair can drift. Jelly must build and ship with this directory deleted.

requires.name: voidcore
requires.note: the model and the dispatcher; Void Squid owns no truth, so every edit is a logged dispatcher command. Reached through Void Maiz's add_subdirectory as the prebuilt libvoidcore.dll, which ships beside the binary. Void Jelly links the same shared Core, so exactly one copy ships.

requires.name: voidmaiz
requires.note: the window, the docking and the widget registry the studio's forms are drawn with (widget_form, project_scene, node_matches), the Session the project is opened through, and the headless front-end (maiz::run_cli). Application chrome (the menus, the workspace bar) is the host's, by Maiz's own line; both Void Hormiga and Void Squid now build the same shell, reported upstream.

requires.name: voidallomone
requires.note: not used directly yet; compiled into Void Maiz, so a change to it is a rebuild here. The game model's derive-only rules (what follows from what, never authored) will use it directly later.

interacts_with.name: voidbicho
interacts_with.note: Planned, and load-bearing for decompilation by the author's decision of 2026-10-10 (okf/design/decompilation.md §8): decompile, name, classify and extract models for the identify and lift stages, embeddings for the shelf, learned perception for the smart log. Invoked through Void Core's effect seam; every output is a proposal. Optional for everything except decompilation's model-assisted stages; nothing links.

interacts_with.name: voidmago
interacts_with.note: Reads this manifest to build the family compatibility matrix.

provides.gui_cli_note: Two executables from one main: `squid` (a console program: the CLI, and the window when run with no command or with a .squid or .ink argument) and `voidsquid` (the same program as a windowed application, for a desktop shortcut). Anything that is not a file argument is Void Maiz's headless front-end over the same HostApp.
provides.effects_note: The build surface (okf/concepts/build-surface.md): every holiday Void Jelly needs a host for. Effects are refused by default and granted per run; --dry-run-effects runs the whole pipeline and writes nothing. artifact-read (2026-10-10) is `effect recon`: the first KiB of one file or a bounded folder listing, plus a PATH lookup per tool, for decompilation's first stage (okf/concepts/recon.md). Two more are planned, an ingress toolchain that invokes readers' tools (REA, ndstool, decomp-toolkit, universal-modder's um) and a hypervisor (for an operating-system artifact), and are not listed until they exist. Added in 0.1.0: `library` (read a library, write the runtime's feast and worlds), `setup` (look at the machine), `loadgame` (recon plus the catalogue), `catalogue` (one network request, on the person's say-so, for the community decompilation list), `play` and `table3d` (start the runtime, a process), `reveal` (the system's file manager). Void MoleRat (2026-10-18) is reached as `effect molerat gather|research|compose|residual|build|status|task|answer|verify`; it uses file-read, file-write and clock, all listed above, and adds no effect kind.

vendors.name: universal-modder
vendors.note: A REFERENCE, not a dependency: nothing compiles, links or runs it from here (third_party/README.md). Pinned at commit 550651675153070cce68066e07c3c8f95df86d08, trimmed of media, upstream agent entry files renamed so they never load into a Void Squid session. The design it informs is okf/design/decompilation.md; whether it becomes a toolchain or a fork is S19. To use um, install it the upstream way; `effect recon` reports whether it is on PATH.

vendors.name: SQLite
vendors.note: reads a library's assets.db; Void Hormiga's copy, unchanged

vendors.name: nlohmann/json
vendors.note: the studio's JSON; Void Hormiga's copy

vendors.name: stb
vendors.note: stb_image (thumbnails, the icon), stb_image_write (the screenshot walk); Void Hormiga's copy

platforms_note: Built and run on windows-x64 (MSYS2 UCRT64) on 2026-10-09 by an agent, with a screenshot. Per Void Maiz's rule a platform joins the array when a GUI binary has run there in front of a person, which has not happened yet. Latin OS is the second host, with no date (okf/concepts/hosts.md).
